newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbia charges Kosovo Albanians with "terrorism".
newsitem.headline: Serbia charges Kosovo Albanians with "terrorism".

text.p: The state prosecutor in Serbia's troubled province of Kosovo has brought charges against 18 ethnic Albanians of terrorism and conspiracy against Yugoslavia, state news agency Tanjug said.
The 18 were members of an illegal organisation, the "National Movement for the Liberation of Kosovo", Tanjug said, adding all but two of the indictees were in prison.

Deputy public prosecutor Jovica Jovanovic said charges were brought on the basis of "evidence of hostile and terrorist activity by the defendants, as well on the basis of the fact that most of them fully admitted their guilt during the investigation". Tanjug did not say when the trial would take place.

Albanian parties deny those arrested were involved in clandestine activities and instead say they are victims of Serbian persecution. Western diplomats say one ethnic Albanian recently died from torture in police custody.
Serbian police cracked down on Kosovo in January, arresting some 70 people in a widely-publicised sweep following a wave of guerrilla attacks over the past year in which more than 30 people died.
The clandestine Kosovo Liberation Army (KLA) was reported to have claimed responsibility for most of the attacks. Albanian parties deny its existence.
Tanjug also said charges were being prepared against more than 20 members of the KLA.

Serbia revoked Kosovo's autonomy in 1989 claiming its Albanian population, outnumbering Serbs nine to one, wants to secede. Albanian deny the claims but want independence from what they describe as a Serbian yoke.
The province is widely regarded as a powder keg that could destroy international peace efforts in the Balkans.
